projects.title: T2FS (TactileThumbFirmSense) Device: A Wearable Thumb Device That is Capable of Sensing Fruit Firmness Using Vision-Based Tactile Sensors
projects.text: TouchRIPE is the UAE’s first wearable, non-destructive device for assessing fruit ripeness, developed, built and patented\ at Khalifa University. It mimics human palpation to measure fruit firmness directly on the tree within seconds, enabling accurate harvest decisions, reducing post-harvest waste, and extending shelf life.

projects.title: PollenMatic: A Compact, Versatile and Low-Cost Device for Efficient Pollination in Greenhouse Cultivation
projects.text: PollenMATIC is a handheld artificial pollination solution designed to provide reliable and controlled pollination in greenhouse crops. The device generates bee-like vibrations that promote pollen release and transfer, helping to improve pollination consistency while reducing dependence on natural pollinators and manual methods

projects.title: Autonomous Weed Detection and Removal in Quinoa Crops.
projects.text: This project develops a modular, AI-enabled laser weeding system for precise, selective, and chemical-free weed management in quinoa cultivation. The system addresses limitations of manual, chemical, mechanical, and row-dependent robotic weeding by enabling targeted weed removal while reducing labor requirements, environmental impact, soil disturbance, and potential crop damage.

projects.title: Robotics-Based Underwater Monitoring
projects.text: The project is developing a heterogeneous marine robotic system that integrates unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) for autonomous inspection and monitoring. By enabling collaboration between these platforms, the system will support persistent autonomy during long-duration marine missions while advancing sustainable ecosystem monitoring, particularly for coral reefs, biodiversity, and overall environmental health.

projects.title: Smart AgriTech Drone for Automated Yield Estimation and Fruit Ripeness Analysis Using Advanced AI-Powered Precision Agriculture Techniques
projects.text: AerialYield is an AI powered precision agriculture platform designed to automate crop monitoring and yield estimation in greenhouse environments. It uses drone and field imagery with computer vision models to detect, count, and classify crops such as blueberries and tomatoes by ripeness stage. The results are integrated into a dashboard to support yield assessment, harvest planning, and data driven farm

projects.title: Plant-AI An Advanced AI Powered Plant Scouting, Disease Detecting and Health Estimating Platform
projects.text: Plant-AI is a Platform, supporting a Mobile App which integrates with a Dashboard. Using Plant-AI Agronomist or Scouting Staff can capture Pictures and Other forms of Data inside various Crops, Plants in Greenhouses or Outdoor Farms. We incorporate SOTA AI Features including:•Advanced Vision Models•Detection Models•Multi-Modal Frameworks•Multi-Ai Agent FrameworksTo Address Plant Health. Primarily we now use Cameras for Analyzing Plant Leaf Health. We aim to use Mobile App Initially to Capture Data and using AI get results in Real-time and showcase all this data, and temporal information and AI based remedies & Suggestions on Greenhouse Monitoring Platform (Dashboard). The goal is Highly Accurate AI based Estimations/Results of Plant Health.This system is trained on real data from UAE based Greenhouses and is primarily built for the Gulf Region environment.

projects.title: The Application of Robotics and AI for Houbara Bustard Conservation
projects.text: The Houbara Robotics and AI Project develops biomimetic robotic systems and intelligent perception tools to support conservation, behavioural monitoring, and assisted breeding. It integrates HuBot, a bird semen collection device, computer vision, bird detection and tracking, vegetation classification, behavioural analysis, autonomous bird tracking, and long-range remote monitoring to enable safer and more efficient conservation operations.

projects.title: SortRIPE: AI-Powered Robotic Fruit Grading System
projects.text: The Fruit Sorting Robot is an intelligent robotic system designed for automated fruit ripeness classification and sorting. The robot integrates a depth camera for 3D visual perception and a robotic stretch arm equipped with a custom gripper and tactile sensor for ripeness assessment. It classifies fruits into categories such as Underripe, Ripe, and Overripe, ensuring accurate, non-destructive quality assessment.

projects.title: TeleRIPE: Constraint-Aware Haptic Guidance for Safe Fruit Harvesting
projects.text: Fruit harvesting requires complex manipulation where fully autonomous robot learning risk violating safety constraints such as joint limits and self-collision. While human guidance can help, existing methods rarely provide clear haptic feedback that prevents issuing unsafe commands. We present a bilateral teleoperation framework that delivers transparent, constraint-aware haptic cues in human-guided robot learning: as the robot nears a safety boundary, a push–pull force is applied to the operator’s hand to discourage unsafe motions. This enables safer and more effective human demonstrations, helping robots learn complex harvesting behaviors while maintaining safety limits.

projects.title: OmniRIPE: A Modular Tactile Device for Continuous Non-Destructive Fruit Firmness and Ripeness Assessment from Farm to Shelf
projects.text: OmniRIPE is a compact, modular fruit assessment device designed for fast, non-destructive firmness and ripeness evaluation from farm to shelf. Using controlled perpendicular palpation, vision-based tactile sensing, and AI, it delivers consistent results across handheld, conveyor, and retail applications, enabling objective harvest, sorting, quality, and shelf-life decisions throughout the supply chain.

projects.title: HumaRipe: A See-Then-Touch Vision–Tactile Cascade for Robotic Tomato Ripeness Assessmenton a Humanoid Mobile Manipulator
projects.text: HumaRipe presents a humanoid mobile manipulation framework for autonomous tomato ripeness assessment in greenhouses. A see-then-touch cascade first uses RGB-D vision to locate and estimate fruit maturity, then dual-arm tactile interaction verifies ripeness. Omnidirectional mobility, LiDAR, and onboard cpu computing enable human-like perception, navigation, inspection, and reliable harvesting decisions.

projects.title: PackRIPE : A Human-Inspired Tactile–Vision Robotic Framework for Postharvest Fruit Handling and Integrated Quality Assessment
projects.text: Quality-aware fruit handling is difficult because robots must localize produce and assess firmness during motion. PackRIPE is a human-inspired closed-loop tactile–vision framework combining AI-based perception, reinforcement-learning grasping, and tactile firmness estimation. Using robotic palpation data from 109 UAE tomatoes, it integrates inspection with handling to support packaging or rejection

projects.title: Teleoperated fruit firmness assessment and harvesting with haptic feedback for precision agriculture
projects.text: TeleRIPE is a VR-based robotic teleoperation system for remote fruit assessment and harvesting. It tracks the operator’s hand movements through a VR headset and WEART haptic gloves, enabling the robotic manipulator and gripper to follow the same movements in real time while providing tactile sensations for natural fruit interaction and ripeness assessment.

projects.title: HealthcareAI: LLM-Guided Medical Data Generation for Intelligent CAD and Clinical Analysis
projects.text: This project develops an LLM-guided framework for generating realistic, structured, and clinically meaningful multimodal medical data to overcome data scarcity in healthcare AI. By synthesizing annotated imaging datasets with controllable disease characteristics, it supports the development, training, validation, and benchmarking of advanced robust computer-aided diagnosis and medical data analysis systems.

projects.title: LLM-Driven Multi-Modal System for Precision Ripeness Mapping and Predictive Harvest Planning in Indoor Densely Fruited Crops
projects.text: PhenoAgent is an LLM-driven multimodal system for precision ripeness mapping, yield estimation, and predictive harvest planning in indoor densely fruited crops. It integrates aerial, mobile, ground-based, and environmental sensing to provide adaptive crop monitoring, ripeness-aware yield prediction, actionable harvesting recommendations, and pre-harvest loss mitigation in GPS-denied farming environments.

projects.title: ProAct-VLM: Pre-Failure Vision-Language Task Replanning with Continuous Perception Feedback
projects.text: ProAct-VLM is an adaptive task-planning framework for dynamic, long-horizon robotic manipulation. It integrates Vision-Language Models with a real-time perception–feedback loop to continuously monitor environmental changes and trigger replanning before failures occur. Evaluations across multiple VLM backbones demonstrate improved task success rates, adaptability, and execution efficiency compared with reactive planning approaches.

projects.title: Coral-CRCA: A Color-Reference Chart Automation algorithm for coral bleaching visualization and severity assessment
projects.text: An algorithm that replicates the visual assessment process used by marine biologists to fully automate coral bleaching evaluation with color-reference charts. The method segments the coral, isolates CoralWatch quadrants, and assigns each coral pixel to the closest reference grade by color similarity, generating pixel-level bleaching visualizations and reporting bleaching percentage.

biography: Dr. Irfan Hussain is an Associate Professor of Robotics and Mechanical Engineering at Khalifa University, Abu Dhabi, UAE, and Deputy Director of the Khalifa University Center for Autonomous Robotic Systems (KUCARS). His research focuses on embodied intelligence, integrating advanced mechanical design, sensing, actuation, compliance, artificial intelligence, perception, planning, learning, and control to develop intelligent robotic systems capable of operating safely and effectively in complex real-world environments. His work spans marine robotics, healthcare robotics, agricultural robotics, wearable robotics, and autonomous systems.

Dr. Hussain received his Ph.D. in Information Engineering, specializing in Automatic Control and Robotics, from the University of Siena, Italy. Prior to joining Khalifa University, he held research positions in Italy, South Korea, and the UAE, building extensive expertise in robotics, control systems, mechatronics, soft robotics, wearable haptics, and compliant robotic systems.

He has authored more than 200 peer-reviewed publications in leading journals and conferences, including IEEE Transactions on Robotics, The International Journal of Robotics Research, Information Fusion, IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, Journal of Field Robotics, and Automatica. His research has attracted thousands of citations and contributed significantly to advancing robotics and autonomous systems. He is also an inventor of multiple U.S. patents, with several technologies progressing toward commercialization.

At Khalifa University, Dr. Hussain leads an internationally recognized research program that has developed innovative robotic technologies, including supernumerary robotic limbs for human augmentation and rehabilitation, compliant exoskeletons, variable-stiffness actuators, tactile sensing systems, autonomous marine robots, and AI-enabled agricultural robots. His work has fostered international collaborations, industry partnerships, advanced laboratory infrastructure, and the training of highly skilled researchers and engineers.

Dr. Hussain actively contributes to the global robotics community through editorial and leadership roles. He has served as Associate Editor for IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), Associate Editor for the Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part C: Journal of Mechanical Engineering Science, Guest Editor for Sensors, and Research Topic Editor for Frontiers in Robotics and AI and Frontiers in Neurorobotics.

His research has received numerous national and international recognitions, including the Khalifa University Research Publication Award, IEEE Haptics Symposium Best Demonstration Award, IEEE ICORR Best Student Paper Finalist recognition, and success at MBZIRC 2024. His work has been featured by CNN, The National, Abu Dhabi Media Office, Wired Middle East, Aspire, and other international media outlets.

Through interdisciplinary research, innovation, mentorship, and collaboration, Dr. Hussain advances next-generation robotic technologies that address critical challenges in healthcare, marine sustainability, food security, and intelligent autonomous systems.
vision: Dr. Hussain's long-term research vision is to advance embodied intelligence in robotic systems through the seamless integration of physical intelligence and cognitive intelligence. Traditional robotics research often separates mechanical design from algorithmic intelligence; however, biological systems achieve adaptability through the interaction between body, sensing, actuation, cognition, and environment.
His work bridges this gap by developing robotic systems that combine compliant design, innovative actuation, intelligent sensing, perception, planning, learning, and control.

This vision has guided the establishment of multiple research programs at Khalifa University, including healthcare robotics, marine robotics, agricultural robotics, wearable robotics, robotic manipulation, and autonomous intelligent systems.

The research philosophy emphasizes both scientific excellence and societal relevance. These technologies address challenges in rehabilitation, human augmentation, food security, environmental sustainability, maritime safety, and industrial automation.
